title: are there books on the technical side of things not just the directing /producer or acting side

commenti.body:
Check your local library (or library via Libby).

Typical recommendations would be something like 'Painting with Light', 'In the Blink of an Eye', and Bordwell's 'Film Art'.

Focal Press puts out a lot of production and post-production related books:

https://www.routledge.com/arts/filmmaking-and-postproduction
Lovely thank you! Any particular recommendations on how to learn to use a camera properly its one of the things i want to learn in particular

I have a friend that started out at our local television station doing in studio filming and live remotes. He eventually got a job at CBS sports filming The Masters,US Open,etc. And this was in a small southern town not a major market. He was lucky that the producer for CBS sports lived locally(married a local) and managed to get the job at CBS through this connection. I also have a nephew that got his first digital hand held camera in middle school which nurtured his interests. He ended up majoring in English/creative writing then went to NYU/Tisch (after interning at a local theatre)and got a Masters in Creative Writing. He is now a successful playwright/scriptwriter/show runner/producer. It takes a while to establish yourself but with perseverance you can succeed. Look into any local stations that may offer internships.

im pretty sure theres some books out there about grip work, i know for sure theres books about gaffing etc. 

i would also recommend asking /r/filmmakers as they probably have better answers

looked it up but theres two books which are related to what youre looking for

Harry C Box - ‘Set Lighting Technicians Handbook’

Michael G. Uva - ‘The Grip Book: Studio Grip’s Essential Guide’

Havent read either but might be what you’re looking for
